title: From a blank file to a first render

steps.say: Every .qmd file starts with a YAML header between two --- lines. A title is enough to render a page.
Below the header you write plain text. Quarto turns it into the page: no styling by hand.
An R chunk runs when you render. Everything it prints lands on the page under it: the tidyverse's start-up notes, readr's messages, and glimpse() of the data.
A second chunk keeps the Kingdom's rows with filter() and draws the chart. It is redrawn on every render, so it always matches the data.

final:
---
title: "Unemployment in the regions"
---

Unemployment fell in most regions between 2022 and 2025.
This note shows the national trend and the latest rates.

## Data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
rates <- read_csv("unemployment.csv")
glimpse(rates)
```

## Trend

```{r}
kingdom <- rates |> filter(region == "Kingdom")
ggplot(kingdom, aes(date, rate)) + geom_line()
```
